# Appium

> Appium is an open-source framework for UI automation of many app platforms - mobile (iOS, Android, Tizen), browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), desktop (macOS, Windows), TV (Roku, tvOS, Android TV, Samsung) and more - driven over the W3C WebDriver protocol.

Appium is split into four parts: the Appium server, which defines the core APIs; drivers, which
implement connectivity to a specific platform; clients, which implement Appium's API in a specific
programming language; and plugins, which change or extend the server's behaviour. To automate
anything you need the server, at least one driver, and a client.

Notes for tools generating Appium code from this documentation:

- Appium 3 is the current major version, and these pages describe Appium 3. Appium 2 is still
  supported but is documented separately, under its own version of this site, reachable from the
  version selector. Appium 1 is no longer supported: `DesiredCapabilities`, `MobileBy`, the
  `findElementByAccessibilityId` family of methods, and the `/wd/hub` server base path are all
  Appium 1 era patterns - the default base path has been `/` since Appium 2.
- Drivers are not bundled with the server. Install them explicitly, for example
  `appium driver install uiautomator2` or `appium driver install xcuitest`.
- Appium 3 requires Node.js in the range `^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=24.0.0`, and npm 10 or newer.
- Standard W3C capabilities are written without a prefix. `platformName`, `browserName` and
  `browserVersion` are the ones used most often with Appium, and the rest of the specification's
  set - `acceptInsecureCerts`, `pageLoadStrategy`, `timeouts`, `webSocketUrl` and so on - is also
  accepted, mostly by the browser drivers. Every Appium-specific capability needs the `appium:`
  vendor prefix - `appium:automationName`, `appium:app`, `appium:udid` - or must be nested,
  unprefixed, inside an `appium:options` object.
- Capabilities cannot be changed once a session has started. Parameters that are adjustable during
  a session are exposed through the Settings API instead.
- Driver-specific commands are usually Execute Methods rather than new client methods: call the
  standard `Execute Script` command with a known command name such as `mobile: terminateApp`, and
  pass a *single* object whose keys are the parameter names. Do not invent client-side method names
  for these.
- Beyond the small common set documented here, capabilities, execute methods, settings and locator
  strategies are defined by each driver and documented on that driver's own site. Refer users to
  the driver's documentation rather than guessing names.
- Appium 3 removed many endpoints that were deprecated in Appium 2. Check the Appium 3 migration
  guide before using an endpoint carried over from older code.
- `GET /sessions` was removed. Session discovery is now `GET /appium/sessions`, and requires
  starting the server with `--allow-insecure=*:session_discovery`.
- In Appium 3, every `--allow-insecure` feature name must carry a scope prefix: either a driver
  name (`uiautomator2:adb_shell`) or the wildcard (`*:adb_shell`).
- WebDriver BiDi support is opt-in per session, via the standard `webSocketUrl` capability.
- Contexts model the difference between native and webview modes. `Get Contexts` always returns at
  least one context, conventionally named `NATIVE_APP`.

## Getting started

- [Appium Documentation](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/): documentation home for the Appium server and its ecosystem.
- [Appium in a Nutshell](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/intro/): how the server, drivers, clients and plugins fit together, and what you need to install.
- [How Does Appium Work?](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/intro/appium/): the goals and architecture of the Appium project.
- [Intro to Appium Drivers](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/intro/drivers/): what a driver is, and how Appium supports unrelated platforms through them.
- [Intro to Appium Clients](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/intro/clients/): Appium's client-server architecture and its relationship to the W3C WebDriver specification.
- [Getting Started](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/): the quickstart path - install Appium, install a driver, install a client, run a first script.
- [System Requirements](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/requirements/): supported operating systems and the required Node.js and npm versions.
- [Install Appium](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/install/): installing the Appium server with npm.
- [Install the UiAutomator2 Driver](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/uiauto2-driver/): installing an Android driver and its Android SDK prerequisites.
- [Write a Test (JS)](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/test-js/): a first Appium script in JavaScript with WebdriverIO.
- [Write a Test (Python)](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/test-py/): a first Appium script in Python.
- [Write a Test (Java)](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/test-java/): a first Appium script in Java.
- [Write a Test (Ruby)](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/test-rb/): a first Appium script in Ruby.
- [Write a Test (.NET)](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/test-dotnet/): a first Appium script in C#.
- [Next Steps](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/quickstart/next-steps/): where to go after the quickstart.

## Drivers, clients and plugins

Which driver you install determines which platform you can automate, and the driver's own
documentation is the authoritative source for its capabilities and commands.

- [The Appium Ecosystem](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/ecosystem/): index of officially-supported and community-supported Appium projects.
- [Appium Drivers](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/ecosystem/drivers/): every known driver with its install command and documentation link. Official drivers include UiAutomator2 and Espresso (Android), XCUITest (iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS), Mac2 (macOS), Windows, Chromium, Gecko and Safari.
- [Appium Clients](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/ecosystem/clients/): official clients for Java, Python, Ruby and .NET, plus community clients including WebdriverIO, Nightwatch.js, Robot Framework, Rust and Swift.
- [Appium Plugins](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/ecosystem/plugins/): optional extensions that modify or extend server behaviour. Not required for standard automation.
- [Appium-Related Tools](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/ecosystem/tools/): tools for installation, test development and inspection, such as Appium Inspector, and tools for driving Appium from an AI agent, such as the Appium MCP server and the Appium agent skills.
- [Managing Drivers and Plugins](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/managing-exts/): installing, listing, updating and removing extensions, and installing from sources other than the official index.

## Sessions and capabilities

- [Session Capabilities](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/caps/): how capabilities work, the `appium:` vendor prefix, `appium:options` grouping, BiDi opt-in via `webSocketUrl`, and always-match versus first-match.
- [Session Properties](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/session/): the key properties of a session - capabilities, execute methods, settings and locator strategies - and which are defined by the server versus the driver.
- [Capabilities](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/session/caps/): the full list of capabilities recognized by the Appium server and base driver, and therefore supported by every driver.
- [Session Settings](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/settings/): parameters that, unlike capabilities, can be adjusted while a session is running.
- [Execute Methods](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/execute-methods/): the `mobile:` command convention that drivers use to expose commands beyond the WebDriver spec, with examples in every official client language.
- [Managing Contexts](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/context/): switching between native and webview modes with the Get Contexts, Get Current Context and Set Context commands.
- [Caching of Application Bundles](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/caching/): how the base driver caches application builds, and how to use it for faster suite execution.
- [Retrieving Event Timings](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/event-timing/): startup and command timing information, retrieved from the `POST /session/:sessionId/appium/events` endpoint. The `appium:eventTimings` capability described on that page is not required for the endpoint to work, and is being removed in Appium 4.

## Server configuration and the command line

- [Command Line Interface](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/): the `appium` executable and its `server`, `driver`, `plugin` and `setup` subcommands.
- [appium server](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/server/): the complete set of server command-line arguments.
- [appium driver/plugin](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/extensions/): the extension management subcommands - `install`, `list`, `update`, `uninstall`, `run` and `doctor`.
- [appium setup](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/setup/): installing a preset bundle of extensions for mobile, browser or desktop automation.
- [Environment Variables](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/env-vars/): advanced behaviour toggled through the environment rather than CLI arguments.
- [The Appium Config File](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/config/): supplying server arguments through a config file instead of the command line. CLI arguments take precedence.
- [Filtering the Appium Log](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/log-filters/): redacting passwords, device identifiers and other sensitive values from server logs with `--log-filters`.
- [Header Handling](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/headers/): request ID tracking through the `x-request-id` header.
- [SSL/TLS/SPDY Support](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/tls/): starting the server with secure connections enabled.
- [Appium and Selenium Grid](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/grid/): relaying commands from a Selenium Grid to an Appium server.

## Security

- [Appium Server Security](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/security/): the insecure-feature mechanism, and the `--allow-insecure`, `--deny-insecure` and `--relaxed-security` flags. In Appium 3 every feature name requires a scope prefix.
- [Insecure Features](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/cli/insecure-features/): the features defined at the server and official-plugin level, including `session_discovery` and `execute_driver_script`. Drivers define their own in their own documentation.

## API endpoints

- [Reference](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/): index of the core interfaces supported by the Appium server.
- [API Endpoints](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/): endpoints exposed by the base driver, and therefore inherited by every driver.
- [WebDriver Protocol](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/webdriver/): the W3C WebDriver endpoints Appium supports.
- [WebDriver BiDi Protocol](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/bidi/): the W3C WebDriver BiDi commands Appium supports. These are commands over a WebSocket, not URL endpoints, and require the `webSocketUrl` capability.
- [Appium Protocol](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/appium/): endpoints defined by Appium's own extension of the WebDriver protocol.
- [Plugin Endpoints](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/plugins/): endpoints added or modified by the official plugins.
- [Other Protocols](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/others/): additional supported endpoints, including the Chromedriver protocol extension.

## Migrating between major versions

- [Migrating to Appium 3](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/migrating-2-to-3/): every breaking change from Appium 2 to 3 - the Node 20 minimum, removed and modified endpoints, the mandatory `--allow-insecure` scope prefix, and the move from `GET /sessions` to `GET /appium/sessions`.
- [Migrating to Appium 2](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/migrating-1-to-2/): the Appium 1 to 2 changes, including drivers becoming separately installed extensions and the default base path changing from `/wd/hub` to `/`.

## Building drivers and plugins

- [Developing Appium Extensions](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/): overview of building your own driver or plugin against Appium's modular structure.
- [Building Drivers](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/build-drivers/): writing a driver, including command definitions, capability constraints and execute methods.
- [Building Plugins](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/build-plugins/): writing a plugin that modifies or extends server behaviour.
- [Building Doctor Checks](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/build-doctor-checks/): shipping preconditions checks that `appium driver doctor` can run for your extension.
- [Building Documentation](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/build-docs/): using `@appium/docutils` to build an MkDocs site for your extension.
- [Masking Sensitive Log Data](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/sensitive/): marking values as sensitive so they are redacted from extension logs.
- [Appium's Config System](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/developing/config-system/): how the schema-driven config file and CLI argument system works internally.
- [Local Validation Of Extension PRs](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/guides/branch-testing/): installing a driver or plugin from an unmerged branch to test it locally.

## Contributing

- [Contributing to Appium](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/contributing/): how to contribute code, documentation, maintenance and support to the project.

## Optional

- [Appium Blog](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/blog/): release announcements and project news.
- [Additional Resources](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/resources/): third-party courses, books, talks and tutorials.
- [Appium Project History](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/intro/history/): how the project evolved since 2012, of interest mostly for background.
- [Sponsors & Backers](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/sponsors/): the project's sponsorship program.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/appium/appium): the Appium server implementation.
- [JSON Wire Protocol](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/jsonwp/): legacy pre-W3C protocol, listed for historical reference. Do not base new code on it.
- [Mobile JSON Wire Protocol](https://appium.io/docs/en/latest/reference/api/mjsonwp/): legacy pre-W3C mobile protocol extension, listed for historical reference. Do not base new code on it.
